column2: I hold counterparties to a standard I don't hold myself to (n=4, also points INWARD)
A threshold fails on its SPEC before it fails on the world; match each leg's window to its own response time
A pre-registration must name an instrument that actually TRADES and a THRESHOLD THAT IS A NUMBER, and "I verified it" is itself a claim that needs running
A continuous front-month ticker (=F) silently re-points at the contract roll — a LEVEL survives it, a DELTA or SPREAD across it is fabricated
A publication date is not an event date — a weekday that disagrees with its date means TWO dates are in play, and that mismatch is the detector
column8: Same field, opposite treatment by direction: DROP the weekday when you AUTHOR an operative instruction (unchecked second assertion); KEEP it when you READ a source (free checksum on their date). No contradiction.

column2: A source that HANGS is not a source that is DOWN — a WAF tarpitting your User-Agent yields TimeoutError, which reads as the publisher's outage and is actually yours
column8: MEASURED at rigcount.bakerhughes.com: identifying UA -> TimeoutError at BOTH 20s and 45s; browser UA -> HTTP 200 in 0.1-0.4s. Cost: a month of aggregator-only BRT-26 grades under a self-authored "primary times out" caveat that hardened into the registry probe field. The fix already existed in probe_gie() one function away, with a comment explaining it. Second, independent error same day: the "primary is a year stale" claim was the ARCHIVE file - both BH link texts contain the words "New Report". Refuted en route and recorded: HTTP/2 was NOT the blocker (both protocols 200 in <0.3s); two variables had been changed at once.

column2: A pathspec-scoped commit after git mv silently drops the half of the rename not in the pathspec - HEAD carries the file at both paths, disk looks fine
column8: The root CLAUDE.md pathspec-scoped commit rule solves a real concurrent-index race and is not retired; this lesson is a NARROW CARVE-OUT for renames only. Two safe patterns: (a) widen pathspec to include BOTH source and destination of every git mv in the commit, or (b) split into a directory-scoped hygiene commit (AGENTS/<YOU>/inbox/) that contains both legs of any rename inside it, followed by a targeted state commit for the rest.
